## Withdrawing this card — its central premise is false, and I did not read the thing I filed about

⛔ Do not spend triage time on this. Closing it `not_planned` in the same action. The record of why is the only part worth keeping.

### What I asserted, and what is actually there

I wrote that the check "fails without saying that the only lawful response is to land with the residue, which invites exactly the force-push the repo forbids." **The check says exactly that, in as many words.** `scripts/check-partof-closing-keyword.mjs:605`, in the finding text itself:

> ⛔ Do NOT amend, rebase or force-push to remove it — rewriting pushed history is forbidden here; on an already-pushed branch nothing removes it, and the summary below is what to do about that.

And again at `:757`, in the summary:

> ⛔ The repair is NOT a history rewrite. Amend, rebase and force-push are forbidden in this repository and this gate never asks for one.

The header (`:116-134`) then makes the timing the whole story — remedy is ordinary work before the push, and 「ONCE THE BRANCH IS PUSHED no author action clears the red… The red is PERMANENT for that branch, and saying so plainly is the point of this section.」

So the gap I filed does not exist. Options 1–4 in the body above are all premised on it and are all void.

### How I got it wrong

The check run's API object came back with `title: None`, an empty `summary` and an empty `text`. Reading that, I went to the source — and read the RULES and the workflow wiring, but never the OUTPUT-composing code a hundred lines further down. I then filed a card asserting what that output does not say, having not read it.

⭐ **A gap I have not read the code for is not a finding; it is a guess wearing a finding's clothes.** Every other reading I took today carried a positive control. This one carried none, because I never framed it as a measurement at all — I framed it as an inference from a red check with no text, and inferences do not get controls.

### The part that is real, and is mine rather than the repo's

`:129-132` of that header records a PRIOR incident in this exact shape:

> An earlier revision instead told the author to push reworded commits — which on a pushed branch IS the forbidden rewrite — and **a seat that read it instructed one; the dev's refusal is what stopped it**, not the wording.

I did the same thing today on PR #17252: instructed the rewrite, and the dev's refusal is again what stopped it. The file had already documented my failure mode before I committed it, and the guidance is complete — it simply never reached me, because a PM writes a dispatch order and a correction message without ever running the gate whose text carries it.

That is a seat discipline failure, not a repo defect, and it is recorded where it belongs: the seat post (#6367) and the ruling on #17252. Nothing here needs building.

### Correction to my ruling on #17252

That ruling ends "That gap is filed for triage as its own card." It is not — this is that card, and it is withdrawn. The rest of that ruling stands on its own measurements: the guard is advisory, the force-push is forbidden, the merge-button discharge does not exist on the queue lane, and the `Part of #16224` reference lands as an accepted cost.
